transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC · Duration: 54 minutes · Attendees: Alyssa (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Priya (Nimbus Head of ML), Liam (Nimbus Cloud), Sofia (Nimbus Security)

Auto-generated Summary: quick demo of scouting flow, ran through 3 candidate open models, looked at bench heur table and compatibility matrix.

Resources mentioned: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/scout-demo (shared), benchmark sheet: https://sheets.goo/example-bench (shared)

[00:00:05] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we said 15:00 UTC, really appreciate you making the time. quick intros?
[00:00:12] Priya: Hi I'm Priya, head of ML at Nimbus Health, we own the triage pipelines and a lot of the clinical summarization work.
[00:00:18] Liam: Liam here -- cloud infra, I'll be looking at networking and costs.
[00:00:21] Sofia: Sofia, security eng, here for SOC2 and data residency Qs.
[00:00:25] Alyssa: Great. Devon and I will run through the "scouting" flow in the Console and then jump to a couple quick benchs. Devon take it away.
[00:00:32] Devon: Yeah thanks. so goal today, show how you'd pick open models for summarization at different token budgets, how to read the compatibility matrix (GPU types, quantization profiles), and show quick benches. i'll share my screen in a sec.
[00:00:45] Priya: Sounds good, our main ask is we want 95% of current quality but at 40-50% lower cost per request if possible. latency under 300ms p50 for short prompts is ideal but we can trade if cost is better.
[00:00:55] Devon: Got it. note that the p50 depends a lot on batch sizing and KV cahce hits, and also whether you run hosted or dedicated.
[00:01:04] Liam: Quick Q — we are leaning private VPC because of PHI, what does Redwood Private look like for network egress and KMS integration?
[00:01:12] Alyssa: Good question. Redwood Private runs customer-controlled control plane in your VPC, you can supply KMS, and audit logs stream to your SIEM. Sofia we can share our private deployment checklist.
[00:01:22] Sofia: We'll want details on key rotation, HSM options, and retention windows in the security pack.
[00:01:28] Alyssa: Absolutely. we'll include SOC2 attestation, ISO paperwork where available.
[00:01:33] Devon: Ok jumping in console. first panel is the model catalog — it's filtered for open models by style: summarization, length, token costs. you can add per-model health and bench columns.
[00:01:45] [00:01:45] Devon: (screen) here's model A — open-llama-13b-quant, compat: A100-80GB, H100, ocp gpus, quantized int4 with recommended profile. accuracy delta vs baseline: -2.1 on our med prompt suite. cost units per 1k tokens: 1.6.
[00:02:05] Priya: That -2.1 is on your med prompt set — can we run it against our in-house sample?
[00:02:09] Devon: Yes, you can upload a sanitized prompt set and run evaluations; that's in the Optimize tab. we'll queue it as a dataset job.
[00:02:15] Priya: Perfect.
[00:02:17] Devon: Next candidate is Model B — flan-xxl-lite, heavier on latency but higher on factuality for clinical notes. compat matrix flags that it needs kernel fallback for some older GPUs, and quantization reduces size but we saw ~3.5% quality drop at int4 profiles.
[00:02:34] Liam: Kernel fallback meaning it might offload some ops to CPU? will that kill latency?
[00:02:38] Devon: It might. the runtime will route to optimized kernels where possible; if your hardware lacks a kernel we'll see CPU fallback for specific ops which can spike latency. we add a "compatibility penalty" column in the matrix so you can see expected perf impact.
[00:02:50] [00:02:50] Priya: How do we compare the models side-by-side quickly?
[00:02:54] Devon: There's a comparison view — you can pin multiple models and see bench rows (throughput/latency/accuracy) and deployment fit. i'll open it.
[00:03:02] Devon: (shows bench) here's a quick bench we ran on A100 vs our Redwood Dedicated pool. note the throughput delta when batch size increases.
[00:03:12] Priya: Is the bench reproducible? we want to run identical runs in our env.
[00:03:16] Devon: Yes, bench config is exportable — we give the run script, kernel flags, and prometheus metrics links. you can clone and run it in Private.
[00:03:24] Sofia: About metrics — are logs and traces PII-free by default? we need to ensure no PHI leaves the environment.
[00:03:29] Alyssa: By default we redact prompt text from some telemetry; for Private deployments you control retention and can set redaction policies. we'll include the config examples.
[00:03:38] [00:03:38] Liam: Cost question — the comp matrix shows a "unit cost" column. how is that calculated?
[00:03:42] Devon: it's a heuristic combining token/sec, average prompt length from your workload, and infra cost of the GPU profile. in Dedicated we give both "amortized per-token" and "real-time p50 cost" estimates.
[00:03:54] Priya: Let's run a quick hypothetical: if we pick Model A quantized and run on Dedicated, what's the expected p50 for 256-token prompts?
[00:04:01] Devon: Roughly 220ms p50 on A100 with our batching defaults, can get to 170ms if you accept slightly higher cost via larger batch lanes. i'll add specific numbers to the bench sheet.
[00:04:12] [00:04:12] Devon: Now show compatibility matrix view — columns: GPU family, quant profiles, kernel level, fallback risk, perf impact %, and recommended deployment mode.
[00:04:22] Priya: Nice. can we filter to show only models that have <3% accuracy drop at int4 and that run on H100?
[00:04:27] Devon: Yep filter builder does that — apply filters, it narrows candidates and shows a scorecard.
[00:04:33] Alyssa: One thing customers like is the "quick simulate" button — it shows estimated monthly cost given your qps and prompt length. we can toggle in the console.
[00:04:41] Liam: For Nimbus we need region-aware routing — some data must stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood pin model serving to region?
[00:04:46] Devon: Yes, routing policies allow region pinning, failover, and tiered fallback. private deployments are isolated to your region by default.
[00:04:54] [00:04:54] Priya: Can the Optimize module suggest quant profiles automatically per model?
[00:04:58] Devon: That's a core feature — Optimize runs model-specific trials and recommends profiles with estimated regressed quality and cost delta. you can accept or tune them.
[00:05:06] Priya: Do you have any heuristics for clinical summarization vs general chat prompts? sometimes hallucination sensitivity is super high for us.
[00:05:12] Devon: Yes we weight factuality metrics higher in the scoring; you can upload label sets for hallucination detection and the system will re-rank models accordingly.
[00:05:20] [00:05:20] Priya: Ok show me a tie-breaker — two models similar cost, one lower latency, one better factuality.
[00:05:24] Devon: The scorecard gives a tuned preference slider — you can move a slider toward latency or quality and we re-score.
[00:05:31] Alyssa: (interrupt) Quick commercial note: if you opt for Dedicated there's a reserved commit discount and we can include a pilot tranche to test your flows before a full migration.
[00:05:39] Liam: What's the min commit for Dedicated?
[00:05:41] Alyssa: Typically starting commitments are 3 months of reserved capacity; flexible options exist depending on workload.
[00:05:47] [00:05:47] Sofia: on security again — do you support customer-managed keys/HSM?
[00:05:50] Devon: Yes KMS/HSM integrations are supported in Private, and Dedicated customers can request customer-keyed encryption for model artifacts.
[00:05:58] Priya: Let's do a short bench run live? we can use a small 10-sample prompt set to get latency numbers.
[00:06:03] Devon: Sure. i'll kick off a quick bench on Model A (quant int4) targeted at an A100 shard in Redwood Dedicated pool. should take ~3-4 minutes.
[00:06:10] [00:06:10] (pause - bench running)
[00:08:30] Devon: Bench done. p50 ~230ms, p95 ~610ms for 256-token prompt, throughput ~24 rps at batch target 4.
[00:08:38] Priya: That's promising. how much of that latency is KV cahce warm vs cold?
[00:08:43] Devon: This run was cold; with prefix caching we typically see p50 improve 15-25% depending on reuse.
[00:08:50] [00:08:50] Priya: Can we simulate our traffic pattern rather than uniform? maybe spikes at 10x.
[00:08:55] Devon: Yes the bench runner can replay traffic patterns and give percentiles under burst. i can add that to the run config.
[00:09:02] Liam: About quantization — if we do int8 rather than int4, what's the delta in cost and accuracy?
[00:09:07] Devon: int8 usually trades off less accuracy drop versus bigger memory — so cost increase compared to int4 but accuracy closer to fp16. typical numbers: int4: -2 to -5% quality, int8: -0.5 to -2%. cost wise int4 ~30-45% lower than fp16, int8 ~15-25% lower.
[00:09:21] [00:09:21] Sofia: For audit we need reproducible quant runs and provenance on model weights — do you store checksums?
[00:09:26] Devon: Yes we store artifact hashes and a provenance record for model imports and quant steps. we'll include an export for compliance review.
[00:09:34] Priya: Any gotchas with tool calling and structured output formats? we rely on JSON-L schema constraints.
[00:09:40] Devon: We support tool calling and structured output. in some quant paths you need to ensure the tokenization and sampling settings are preserved. we test serializer behavior in the compatibility matrix.
[00:09:51] Alyssa: I'm going to summarize next steps so we're aligned. first, Priya will share a sanitized sample set. Devon will run a longer bench (1k token, burst sim) and add results to the shared sheet. I'll send pilot pricing and SOW.
[00:10:03] Priya: Yep that's right.
[00:10:05] [00:10:05] Devon: quick note: we also recommend running a 2-week canary in Dedicated with fallback policies and tracing enabled before full cutover.
[00:10:12] Priya: Sounds sensible.
[00:10:15] Liam: Ok when can we do the infra Q&A? next week works for us.
[00:10:19] Alyssa: I'll propose a slot for 2026-07-27.
[00:10:23] [00:10:23] Sofia: Can you share the security pack now or after? prefer now so we can triage.
[00:10:28] Alyssa: We'll send it after the call; it's in the docs link I'll include in the follow-up.
[00:10:33] Priya: Quick question on model updates — if an open model upstream releases a patch, how are rollouts managed?
[00:10:39] Devon: We support pinning versions and staged rollouts: canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback. for open models we validate compatibility in a staging run before promoting.
[00:10:49] [00:10:49] (several people talk)
[00:11:05] Priya: One more — can the Console surface per-prompt cost attribution for debugging?
[00:11:09] Devon: Yes, token-level breakdowns per request and cost attributions show in the Console. you can filter by route, model, and token-type.
[00:11:18] Alyssa: ok we're about out of time. recap: Priya share sample and acceptance criteria; Devon run extended benches and add to sheet; Alyssa send pricing and security pack; schedule infra Q&A on 7/27.
[00:11:30] Priya: thanks everyone.
[00:11:32] Alyssa: Thanks all.

Action items (auto):
- Priya: share sanitized dataset to drive Optimize evals.
- Devon: bench runs + upload results to shared bench sheet.
- Alyssa: follow-up email with pricing, SOW, and security pack.

End of transcript.
